stops.note: 'comfort of the throat', the source of Turkish 'lokum'
the confectioner Hacı Bekir opened his Istanbul shop in 1777, and his lokum became famous across Europe
coined in English for lokum; C. S. Lewis's 'The Lion, the Witch and the Wardrobe' (1950) made it famous

current_meaning: a sweet of starch and sugar gel, flavoured and dusted with icing sugar
